study_identification_part.si4_title: Multiscale heterogeneity of functional connectivity in autism

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To use normative modelling to characterize the inter-individual heterogeneity of functional connectivity (FC) in autism at the level of pair-wise inter-regional connections, specific brain regions, and broader functional networks, and to investigate the clinical relevance of these deviations.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The paper describes the key steps for creating the functional connectivity matrices, including parcellation, correlation, normalization, and harmonization.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: To map inter-regional FC, we used the well-validated Schaefer parcellation (Schaefer et al., 2018) to obtain 400 functional cortical regions of interest (ROIs) for each participant. We also included 15 subcortical ROIs from the Harvard-Oxford subcortical atlas... We used Pearson correlations to calculate the relationship between each pair of regional average time series. We then normalized the values within each participant's FC matrix using Gaussian-gamma mixture modeling... We used ComBat (Johnson, Li, & Rabinovic, 2007) to regress the scan-site-specific effects from the FC data...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Support vector regression (SVR) was used to develop multivariate predictive models of clinical and cognitive measures (ADOS, ADI, SRS, IQ, SSP, AQ) from FC deviation scores at connection, region, and network levels. A five-fold cross-validation procedure was used with PCA for dimensionality reduction (retaining 50% of variance).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Autistic individuals show highly heterogeneous functional connectivity deviations at the single-connection level, but these deviations converge on common sensory-motor (negative deviations) and transmodal (positive deviations) brain networks, and these multi-scale deviation patterns predict clinical and cognitive scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study found extreme heterogeneity in functional connectivity at the single-connection level (no more than 3.4% overlap in either group), but greater convergence at coarser scales. Autistic individuals showed significantly greater overlap for negative deviations (reduced FC) in sensory-motor, insular, and prefrontal regions, and for positive deviations (increased FC) in medial prefrontal, cingulate, and inferior parietal regions. At the network level, negative deviations converged on visual, attention, and somatomotor-related connections, while positive deviations converged on DMN, cognitive control, and subcortical connections. These deviation patterns predicted clinical scores; for example, single-connection deviations predicted IQ (r=0.16) and SRS (r=0.29), while network-level deviations predicted ADI social (r=0.17) and SRS (r=0.18).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: 1. Exclusion of the cerebellum due to poor scan coverage in a large portion of participants. 2. Imbalanced sex ratio between the autism and control groups.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Due to poor scan coverage in a large portion of the participants, our analysis did not include the cerebellum... Our sample also had an imbalanced sex ratio between the autism and control groups, which aligns with the higher prevalence of autism in males compared to females.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study employed a multi-scale analysis, investigating FC deviations at the connection, region, and network levels to bridge findings of heterogeneity and commonality. It also used an AUC-based permutation testing approach to compare group overlap across a range of thresholds, enhancing robustness compared to single-threshold methods.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study is a preprint and has not undergone peer review. The authors make supplementary materials and data available through various repositories (EU-AIMS, ABIDE), but the supplementary document itself was not included with the provided markdown file.
